title: Rabbi Abba of Caesarea
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Taanit 15b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.15b.15), but the reading of the Rif and Dikdukei Soferim there is Rabbi Ada. In [Moed Katan 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.20b.4) he recited a baraita before Rabbi Yochanan, according to the reading of the She’iltot, Vayechi, the Rosh there and Dikdukei Soferim; the reading Hyman uses is Rabbi Ada of Caesarea. In [Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Rosh_Hashanah.4.4.3): Rabbi Abba of Caesarea said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan.[^2]

notes.text: The baraita-reciter role and Jerusalem Talmud locations are made explicit. The supplied names and attribution chains remain distinct.

Taanit names Abba in the discussion of ashes on a fast day, which [continues on 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.16a.1). The consulted Moed Katan and Yerushalmi passages both name Ada. Heilprin lists [Abba](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=21&lang=en) and [Ada](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=215&lang=en) separately and raises the possibility of a name variant. Hyman’s readings from the Rif, She’iltot, Rosh and Dikdukei Soferim remain his reports here.
